s1.syndrome_frame: Acute monocular vision loss with orbital and adnexal signs
salient_findings: Pain, numbness, and erythema of the eyelids and forearm
Tense eyelid edema, chemosis, and corneal haze
key_facts: Obese man in his mid-30s
No prior systemic or ocular disorders
Heavy alcohol consumption the night prior
Took 2 buprenorphine hydrochloride/naloxone hydrochloride pills
Denies any trauma
Visual acuity: No light perception in right eye, 20/20 in left eye
Intraocular pressure: 37 mm Hg in right eye, 21 mm Hg in left eye
Creatinine level: 2.2 mg/dL
Creatine kinase level: 29,320 U/L
Periorbital soft-tissue swelling on noncontrast computed tomography
Severe disorganization of the retinal architecture on Optical Coherence Tomography
Delayed choroidal filling and poor vascular perfusion on Fluorescein Angiography

shortlist.label: Central retinal artery occlusion
shortlist.why_kept: Sudden vision loss in one eye with retinal findings

shortlist.label: Acute angle-closure glaucoma
shortlist.why_kept: High intraocular pressure and vision loss in one eye

shortlist.label: Purtscher-like retinopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Retinal findings and trauma-like presentation without actual trauma

shortlist.label: Orbital compartment syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Periorbital swelling and increased intraocular pressure

shortlist.label: Cavernous sinus thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Severe vision loss and potential for orbital and adnexal signs

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of vision loss, periorbital edema, and retinal findings such as serous retinal detachment and macular whitening, combined with the elevated creatine kinase level suggesting rhabdomyolysis, is consistent with Purtscher-like retinopathy, which can occur in the setting of severe systemic disease or trauma, including rhabdomyolysis.

rejected.label: Central retinal artery occlusion
rejected.why: While it could explain vision loss, it does not account for the systemic findings and periorbital edema.

rejected.label: Acute angle-closure glaucoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with severe eye pain, headache, and nausea, which are not the primary complaints here, and the intraocular pressure, although elevated, is not as high as typically seen in acute angle-closure glaucoma.

rejected.label: Orbital compartment syndrome
rejected.why: Could explain some of the findings like periorbital edema and increased intraocular pressure, but the retinal and systemic findings point more towards a diagnosis like Purtscher-like retinopathy.

rejected.label: Cavernous sinus thrombosis
rejected.why: Would likely present with more profound neurologic deficits and bilateral involvement, which is not seen in this case.
